item.title: Trump Says He Wants AI Guardrails, But ‘As Little as Possible’
item.description: President Donald Trump said he sees the need for some standards on artificial intelligence technology, but wants to avoid burdensome restrictions that may hamper American companies competing with China.

item.title: Asian Stocks to Fall a Second Day on Tech Worries: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were set to decline for a second session as investors continued to rotate out of technology shares on concerns that the artificial intelligence-fueled rally has run ahead of itself.

item.title: Oil Steadies as More Supply Flows Through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Oil steadied as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased further, adding to a gush of near-term supply while talks between the US and Iran continue.

item.title: Trump Says Fed’s Warsh Faces Board That’s a ‘Bit Hostile’
item.description: President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh may not be able to compel his colleagues on the central bank to do what the new chair wants on monetary policy.

item.title: Crusoe in Talks to Raise $3 Billion in Round That May Triple Firm’s Value
item.description: Crusoe, the data center upstart with contracts to supply AI computing power for the likes of Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp., is in talks to raise about $3 billion in a funding round that may triple the company’s valuation, people familiar with the situation said.

item.title: Canada, Philippines Agree to Sign Trade Deal This Year, Grow Defense Ties
item.description: Canada and the Philippines plan to finalize a free trade agreement this year, and signed agreements to deepen cooperation on energy, defense, labor and migration, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Thursday.

item.title: 【今朝の5本】仕事を始める前に読んでおきたい厳選ニュース
item.description: ​米雇用統計、海峡通航料、インサイダー疑惑、AIチップ製造パートナー、キーウ攻撃

item.title: South Korea Opens 24-Hour Won Trading at a Fraught Moment
item.description: Deep inside a government complex in Sejong, about two hours from Seoul, a room known as “the box” is ground zero for South Korea’s currency anxieties.

item.title: World’s Worst-Performing Exchange ASX Bets on Outsider for Pivot
item.description: When Anthony Attia takes the helm at Australia’s ASX Ltd., the world’s worst-performing stock exchange operator, he’ll need to launch straight into a battle to win over regulators and investors.

item.title: Los conciertos de Bad Bunny muestran cómo la migración latina está impulsando la economía de España
item.description: En los últimos tres años, el país ha acogido a más de tres millones de personas, muchas de ellas procedentes de América Latina. Estas personas han contribuido a convertir a España en la economía de la eurozona de más rápido crecimiento.

item.title: Wall Street Bets Rallying Markets Will Absorb Every Market Blow
item.description: Wall Street is kicking off the second half of 2026 with fresh conviction: shrugging off one shock after another, markets are set to grind even higher.

item.title: FBI Probes Whether Alarum Unit Is Behind Co-Opted Home Devices
item.description: The FBI is investigating whether a subsidiary of the data-collection firm Alarum Technologies Ltd. had a role in linking customers’ home internet devices without their consent into a network that people can use to disguise their locations, according to documents seen by Bloomberg News and confirmed by people familiar with the situation.

item.title: Software Developers Rethink Apps for Their Newest Users: AI Agents
item.description: Potential adjustments range from rethinking pricing and permissions to overhauling designs

item.title: Spotify Challenges Prediction Markets After Song Chart Rigging
item.description: Spotify has asked Kalshi and Polymarket to remove its logo and clarify that neither company has a partnership with the streaming service after it identified users manipulating rankings that are tied to prediction market bets.

item.title: Ramaphosa Calls for $1.5 Billion Ebola Pledges to Be Funded
item.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa urged African leaders and international partners to make good on their $1.5 billion in Ebola assistance pledges.

item.title: Brown University’s Rating Outlook Lowered to Negative by Moody’s
item.description: Brown University had the outlook on its credit rating lowered to negative on Thursday by Moody’s Ratings, which cited expense pressures facing the institution.

item.title: Barclays Pulls Near $1 Billion Debt Deal for Sound Physicians
item.description: Barclays Plc has withdrawn a near $1 billion financing for Sound Inpatient Physicians Inc. from the debt capital markets, marking one of the few leveraged loan deals to be pulled this year.

item.title: Invesco’s Brill Gives SpaceX Bond a Red Card for ‘Very Sloppy’ Performance
item.description: Invesco Advisers Inc.’s head of investment-grade credit for North America slammed SpaceX’s inaugural bond sale on Thursday for a “very sloppy” secondary market performance.

item.title: JPMorgan Loses Battle Over Charlie Javice’s Legal Expenses
item.description: A Delaware judge said JPMorgan Chase & Co. failed to show that Charlie Javice‘s $74 million in legal fees were clearly excessive, ruling the bank must continue to pay her bills.

item.title: Warsh’s Calendar in First Week as Fed Chair Shows Staff Meetings
item.description: Kevin Warsh’s calendar for his first week in office as Federal Reserve chairman shows a diary that was mostly busy with internal staff meetings, with the exception of a handful of others that included breakfast with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

item.title: Genuine Parts Is Said to Receive O’Reilly Interest for Auto Unit
item.description: Genuine Parts Co. has attracted a cash bid for its auto-parts arm from O’Reilly Automotive Inc. as it seeks to refocus on its industrials business, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Top ‘Suicide Squad’ Developers Say the Flop Made Them Not Want to Make Games Anymore
item.description: The director and top designer of Rocksteady’s failed game open up about their experiences

item.title: Ishbia’s Mortgage Takeover Attempt Fails, Ending Monthslong Feud
item.description: After months of delay and drama, shareholders of mortgage servicer Two Harbors Investment Corp. voted to approve a merger deal with CrossCountry Mortgage Thursday. The preliminary vote was a blow to Mat Ishbia’s UWM Holdings Corp., which was also courting Two Harbors as an antidote to its severe stock slide.

item.title: The Doves Have Already Left the Building
item.description: A hawkish pivot was brewing before Warsh’s ascension.

item.title: ElevenLabs in Talks for Tender Offer at $22 Billion Valuation
item.description: ElevenLabs has held early talks with investors to let employees sell shares in a secondary offering that would value the artificial intelligence startup at roughly $22 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Refiner Profits Are Soaring in Sign of Lingering Hormuz Snarls
item.description: US crude refiners are enjoying some of the best profit margins in years, the latest sign that even as energy shipments pick up through the Strait of Hormuz, there are lingering supply-chain kinks still rippling through global markets.

item.title: Trump Financial Disclosure Shows 21,000 Trades in 2025
item.description: President Donald Trump made more than 21,000 securities trades in his first year back in office, often in intense bursts tied to market events he created.

item.title: Carney Keeps North BC Tanker Ban, Signaling Alberta’s Pipeline Will Go South
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced a deal with British Columbia that keeps an oil tanker ban in place for Canada’s north coast, and commits billions of dollars in federal funding for energy, mining and transportation projects.

item.title: German Reform Plan Could Lift 2027 GDP Above 1%, Merz Tells ARD
item.description: The package of reforms just laid out by Germany’s coalition could lift the nation’s GDP above 1% in 2027, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told ARD.

item.title: Prison Phone Company Aventiv Clears Hurdle for Lenders’ Takeover
item.description: Aventiv Technologies has clinched an out-of court deal for lenders to take control of the prison phone company from private equity firm Platinum Equity, capping a lengthy slog to clear regulatory approval, according to people familiar with the matter.
